subject: Forest loss in India — three sources, and only two of them are available
kind_note: Forest cover is measured from satellite imagery classified by canopy density. It is a measurement, not a model — but the CLASS boundaries are a definition, and the definition is where the disagreement lives.

limit.what_it_requires: Forest land may not be used for a non-forest purpose without prior approval of the central government. Approval is normally conditional on compensatory afforestation and payment of the net present value of the land.
limit.why_it_is_not_a_number: The Act does not cap how much forest may be diverted. It caps who may decide. So this page cannot say "the limit was exceeded" — it can only say how much was approved, and that figure is published by the Ministry rather than by FSI.
limit.hole: Diversion approvals under the Act are not in ISFR and were not obtained for this build. Until they are, the page states the requirement and not a quantity.

a_india.role: India's own official assessment — the primary source
a_india.name: Forest Survey of India, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
a_india.publication: India State of Forest Report 2023, Volume 1

b_international.role: the international series — and NOT an independent check
b_international.name: Forest area (sq. km)
b_international.upstream: Food and Agriculture Organization, Global Forest Resources Assessment
b_international.not_independent: The World Bank republishes FAO, and FAO republishes what each country reports. For India that is FSI. So source B agreeing with source A is not corroboration; it is the same measurement travelling.

c_satellite.name: Hansen / UMD tree cover loss, via Global Forest Watch
c_satellite.says: tree cover loss, in millions of hectares since 2000
c_satellite.what_it_would_add: Annual tree-cover loss for India from the Hansen/UMD satellite series — the one measurement on this page that is not derived from what the Government of India reports about itself. It is the source that disagrees, so it is the source that matters most.

probe.message: Request is missing valid API key. Please see documentation at https://data-api.globalforestwatch.org/#tag/Authentication on how to create one.

c_satellite.how_to_close: Create a Global Forest Watch API key and set GFW_API_KEY. One account, free. It was deliberately not created during this build.

the_disagreement.headline: India's own report says its forest cover grew. The satellite series says India has lost tree cover. Both can be true, and the reason is the definition.
why: Forest cover counts canopy above 10 per cent density on land over one hectare, whatever is growing there. A plantation counts. An orchard can count.
Tree cover loss counts canopy disappearing, whatever it was. A harvested plantation is a loss.
So a natural forest replaced by a plantation of the same canopy density is NO CHANGE to the first measure and a LOSS AND GAIN to the second. Neither number is wrong.

the_number_that_survives_either_definiti.claim: A national net change of 156.41 km2 is smaller than the loss in a single state.
the_number_that_survives_either_definiti.source: both figures are from ISFR 2023, Table 2.2 and the paragraph following it
the_number_that_survives_either_definiti.note: This is division on two numbers in one table. It needs no second source and it survives any argument about definitions.

caveats: Two sources agreeing is not corroboration when one is the other's input.
A net change conceals gross gain and gross loss, and ISFR publishes no national gross figure.
A change of two hundredths of one per cent is inside what a change of mapping method can produce.
"Forest cover" is a canopy measurement, not an ecosystem measurement, and includes plantations.
A failed fetch is recorded as null. It is never recorded as zero forest.
The missing satellite source is named with its actual API response, not described from memory.
